identification.name: E-Glass / Epoxy (Woven, NEMA G-10)
identification.common_form_notes: Available as FR-4 (a flame-retardant grade designation) / NEMA (National Electrical Manufacturers Association) G-10 laminate sheet from electrical/insulation suppliers. Machines well with carbide tooling; avoid excessive heat during cutting to prevent delamination.
identification.notes: Woven E-glass fabric / epoxy laminate to NEMA Grade G-10 (equivalently MIL-I-24768/2 Type GEE). Properties are in-plane (warp/fill); a balanced weave makes the two directions similar but not identical - where a source distinguishes them: tensile strength 262 MPa crosswise / 310 MPa lengthwise (MatWeb/Boedeker, ASTM D638) vs. a single 275 MPa MIL-spec value (Atlas Fibre); flexural modulus 16.5 GPa crosswise / 18.6 GPa lengthwise (ASTM D790); CTE 9.9 um/m.K lengthwise / 11.9 crosswise (ASTM D696, 20 C). youngs_modulus stores the crosswise (more conservative) flexural modulus - these datasheets publish no tensile modulus for G-10, so the ASTM D790 flexural value is used as the modulus of elasticity. tensile_strength, compressive_strength (448 MPa - corrected from an earlier 300 MPa estimate; Atlas Fibre and MatWeb agree), shear_strength (131 MPa in-plane, ASTM D732) and Rockwell M 110 hardness are from the Atlas Fibre MIL-I-24768/2 data sheet. Through-thickness tensile and interlaminar shear strengths are much lower than in-plane values (typically 30-50 MPa) - design against delamination in peel or through-thickness loading. von Mises shear derivation does not apply to a composite; the stored shear_strength is the measured in-plane value. The epoxy matrix is a thermoset: no melting point. usable_temp_range upper bound (140 C) is Atlas Fibre's stated maximum operating temperature (MatWeb agrees); the published matrix glass transition is ~130 C (makeitfrom.com). The -60 C lower bound is a conservative service figure retained from the earlier makeitfrom.com data - G-10 is used structurally to cryogenic temperatures, but none of these datasheets give a low-temperature rating. Not suitable for sustained loads at elevated temperature without specific creep data. Ductility values are strain to fracture (brittle failure); there is no plastic yield. electrical_conductivity is nominally 0% IACS - G-10 is a high-performance electrical insulator (dielectric strength ~31.5 kV/mm, dielectric constant ~5.0 at 1 MHz), not a specific sourced measurement. specific_heat (1000 J/kg.K) is a rough estimate and remains unsourced; thermal_conductivity (0.288 W/m.K, ASTM C177) and the other values above are sourced to the Atlas Fibre and MatWeb datasheets.

typical_usage: Electrical insulation panels and PCB (printed circuit board) substrates (FR-4), structural laminates in moisture-sensitive environments, jigs and fixtures, tooling plates, machine guards, and general-purpose composite sheet where moderate stiffness, electrical insulation, and low cost are required.
